content:
Online media '胡‧說樓市' reported on Friday (the 2nd) that a detached house valued over HK$100 million at One Stanley in Stanley has steel reinforcement quality issues. Analysis of the steel reinforcement quantity in certain locations shows it is approximately 41% to 75% less than the approved plans. The Buildings Department stated on Saturday (the 3rd) that it had received a report and, after inspection, found that the protective layer of a beam on the ground low level was not fitted with wire mesh as required by the plans, and the steel reinforcement configuration of some floor slabs did not match the plans. According to '胡‧說樓市', the developer, Kinhoo Real Estate, had sent a lawyer's letter requesting the suspension or cessation of the report's publication, stating that 'if unverified allegations affect the project's sales, we reserve the right to pursue legal liability.' The vendor of One Stanley, Kin Way Limited, issued a statement last night expressing that it takes the matter very seriously and will follow up rigorously. If any lapses are found after investigation, it will certainly carry out remedial works for the affected property in accordance with the law, and pursue the responsibility of the relevant parties.

Developer: Kinhoo Real Estate　Contractor: Hoi Yuet Construction

128 Wong Ma Kok Road, Stanley, is a low-density luxury residence. The entire development comprises only 82 units, including 32 houses and 11 low-rise residential blocks. The developer is Kinhoo Real Estate, and the contractor is Hoi Yuet Construction Engineering, a subsidiary of China State Construction Engineering (Hong Kong). Kinhoo Real Estate was established in 2013, founded by the father-and-son duo Lo Ka-kui and Lo Kin-yat, who are descendants of the Bossini family.

'胡‧說樓市' has been following the incident for over half a year. The report stated that the unit owner purchased the unit in April 2024 and, during renovations in August last year, discovered that the surface concrete of some floor slabs was abnormal. The plaster surface layer below the floor of the master bedroom on the second floor had peeled off, and it was subsequently found that the steel reinforcement was 'out of position' with uneven spacing.

The report stated that after the Buildings Department conducted scanning and removal tests, the registered structural engineer commissioned by the owner, based on the Buildings Department's data analysis, pointed out that the quantity of main steel reinforcement in certain locations of the study on the second floor was approximately 41% to 75% less than the approved plans; and in certain locations of the bedroom ceiling on the first floor, it was approximately 42% to 57.9% less.

Buildings Department issued 'Occupation Permit' in July 2023

In response to '胡‧說樓市''s report, the Buildings Department stated that it had received a report and has been following up on the investigation seriously. The Buildings Department pointed out that the detached house was issued an 'Occupation Permit' in July 2023, and the owner carried out renovations after purchase. The Buildings Department received a report from the owner's representative in January this year regarding the structural safety of the floor slabs inside the house. After an on-site inspection in March, it considered that the overall building structure did not pose obvious danger. The department wrote to the project's registered structural engineer requesting the submission of relevant material test reports and certificates.

Buildings Department: Steel reinforcement configuration of some floor slabs does not match the plans

The Buildings Department stated that it conducted multiple inspections from June to September this year, carrying out concrete strength rebound hammer tests, surface thickness gauge surveys, surface radar surveys for steel reinforcement configuration, core drilling compression tests, and on-site opening inspections, and is currently analysing the data. The Buildings Department stated that the tests and inspections found that the protective layer of a beam on the ground low level of the detached house was not fitted with wire mesh as required by the plans; in addition, the steel reinforcement configuration of some floor slabs did not match the plans.

Wrote to developer etc. requesting assistance in investigation

The Buildings Department stated that these situations 'do not constitute obvious danger' and will be further investigated. The department has written to the project's developer, contractor, authorised person, and registered structural engineer, requesting assistance in the investigation. The Buildings Department reminded the industry that, in accordance with the Buildings Ordinance, building professionals and contractors must supervise and carry out construction in accordance with the approved plans. The department also stated that if it is found after investigation that any building professionals and contractors have violated the Buildings Ordinance, it will definitely follow up rigorously, including initiating prosecution and/or disciplinary action.

Vendor: Will give a timely account after gathering and verifying more information

Kin Way Limited, the vendor of One Stanley, responded that it takes the matter very seriously and will follow up rigorously. The company stated that, according to information released by the Buildings Department, the Buildings Department considers that the overall building structure of the property does not pose obvious danger. Kin Way stated that it is currently understanding and verifying the details in detail, and will do its best to cooperate with the Buildings Department's investigation, and will give a timely account after gathering and verifying more information. If any lapses by any parties in construction quality or other related matters are found after investigation, it will certainly carry out remedial works for the affected property in accordance with laws and regulations, and pursue the responsibility of the relevant parties in accordance with the law.
